actions.name: developed Snake implant
actions.description: The FSB began developing Snake as “Uroburos” in late 2003. Development of the initial versions of the implant appeared to be completed around early 2004.

actions.name: used Snake implant for cyber espionage
actions.description: The FSB has used Snake to collect sensitive intelligence from high-priority targets, such as government networks, research facilities, and journalists.

actions.name: used Snake implant to exfiltrate sensitive international relations documents
actions.description: FSB actors used Snake to access and exfiltrate sensitive international relations documents, as well as other diplomatic communications, from a victim in a NATO country.

actions.name: targeted industries in the United States with Snake implant
actions.description: Within the United States, the FSB has victimized industries including education, small businesses, and media organizations, as well as critical infrastructure sectors including government facilities, financial services, critical manufacturing, and communications.

actions.name: deployed Snake to external-facing infrastructure nodes
actions.description: The FSB typically deploys Snake to external-facing infrastructure nodes on a network, and from there uses other tools and TTPs on the internal network to conduct additional exploitation operations.

actions.name: obtained administrator credentials and accessed domain controllers
actions.description: Upon gaining and cementing ingress into a target network, the FSB typically enumerates the network and works to obtain administrator credentials and access domain controllers.

actions.name: used keyloggers, network sniffers, and open source tools to gather credentials
actions.description: A wide array of mechanisms has been employed to gather user and administrator credentials in order to expand laterally across the network, to include keyloggers, network sniffers, and open source tools.

actions.name: deployed small remote reverse shell with Snake
actions.description: FSB operators sometimes deploy a small remote reverse shell along with Snake to enable interactive operations. This triggerable reverse shell can be used as a backup access vector or to maintain a minimal presence in a network and avoid detection while moving laterally.

actions.name: used Snake kernel module to conceal host components
actions.description: Snake utilizes the kernel module to mediate any requests between Snake’s user mode components and the concealed storage mechanism, which itself is encrypted with a unique per-implant key. The kernel module removes relevant components from any listing returned by the operating system.

actions.name: maintained persistence via Windows service named WerFaultSvc
actions.description: The Snake version primarily discussed registers a service named WerFaultSvc to maintain persistence. On boot, this service executes Snake’s WerFault.exe, which decrypts Snake’s components and loads them into memory.

actions.name: decrypted encrypted registry blob to obtain AES key, IV, and path for kernel driver
actions.description: Snake’s WerFault.exe attempts to decrypt an encrypted blob within the Windows registry at HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Classes\.wav\OpenWithProgIds. The encrypted data includes the AES key, IV, and path used to find and decrypt the file containing Snake’s kernel driver and loader.

actions.name: dropped kernel driver and custom DLL loader in encrypted file comadmin.dat
actions.description: Snake’s installer drops the kernel driver and a custom DLL used to load the driver into a single AES encrypted file named comadmin.dat stored in %windows%\system32\Com directory.

actions.name: used Queue File to store key material, communication channels, and operational data
actions.description: The Queue is a Snake structure saved on disk in the Queue File, containing key material, communication channels, modes of operation, and principal user mode component data required for operation.

actions.name: used custom encrypted network communications over HTTP, TCP, UDP, SMTP, and DNS
actions.description: Snake’s network communications are encrypted, fragmented, and sent using custom methodologies over common protocols including raw TCP and UDP sockets and higher-level protocols like HTTP, SMTP, and DNS.

actions.name: used kernel module to intercept TCP sessions and authenticate Snake traffic without opening new ports
actions.description: Snake kernel module intercepts the first client-to-server packet following the TCP 3-way handshake and authenticates it using the per-implant ustart value. If valid, the kernel module forwards packets to Snake processing without opening new ports or interfering with legitimate applications.
actions.epistemic_reason: 原文以不確定語氣陳述（如 may have／appears to／we believe），不是已確認的事實。

actions.name: used ustart authentication technique with nonce and hash for network traffic authentication
actions.description: Snake uses the ustart authentication technique involving sending a random nonce and a mathematical operation on the nonce and ustart value to authenticate sending machines. The receiving machine performs the same computation to authenticate.

actions.name: used DNS queries and responses for outbound and inbound communications
actions.description: Snake encodes information in seemingly standard DNS queries for outbound communications and parses returned IPv4 addresses in DNS responses as covert channel data for inbound communications.

actions.name: used custom HTTP protocols (http and http2) for network communications
actions.description: Snake uses custom HTTP protocols riding on standard HTTP, with client-to-server data contained in HTTP header fields or POST bodies, employing base62 encoding and including ustart authentication in every client-to-server communication.

actions.name: used custom TCP protocol with length-prefixed commands and ustart authentication
actions.description: Snake’s custom TCP protocol uses length-prefixed commands with a 32-bit big-endian length field, performs ustart authentication once per TCP session, and exchanges length-data pairs for commands and responses.

actions.name: used enc layer with Diffie-Hellman key exchange and pre-shared key for session encryption
actions.description: Snake’s enc layer establishes a unique session key through a Diffie-Hellman key exchange combined with a pre-shared key stored in the implant’s Queue, used to encrypt command headers and payloads.

actions.name: processed Snake commands with modular design allowing new commands
actions.description: Snake’s Application Layer processes commands differentiated as High (ordinal >= 0x64) and Low commands, with modular design allowing operators to add new commands by remotely loading modules.

actions.name: executed commands to gather system information and manipulate files
actions.description: Operators used commands such as PS to list processes, List Dir to list directory contents, Syst to gather system info, Kill to terminate processes, Get to exfiltrate files, Put to write files, Del to delete files, and Run to execute shell commands.

actions.name: used Queue commands to enumerate, read, write, and delete Queue Items
actions.description: Snake commands with ordinals 0xa, 0xb, 0xc, and 0xd are used to enumerate, read, write, and delete items from the 0x0 or 0x1 Queue Containers respectively.

actions.name: used Forward commands to relay commands through multiple hop points
actions.description: Forward commands (ordinal 0x1) instruct an implant to forward a Snake command to a second target node, creating chains of hop points that forward commands to an end point, with responses returned back through the chain encrypted end-to-end.

actions.name: conducted Active operations issuing commands with immediate response
actions.description: During Active operations, Snake commands are issued by an FSB operator or script to a target machine, generally through Forward commands, with responses immediately returned to the origin.

actions.name: conducted Passive operations with implants beaconing and exchanging commands asynchronously
actions.description: During Passive operations, Snake implants operate autonomously, beaconing randomly to stored communication channels with Queue Read commands to retrieve commands, executing them, and exfiltrating data with Queue Write commands to random stored channels.

actions.name: used memory injection of user mode component into chosen process
actions.description: Snake’s principal user mode component is injected into a chosen process via a single allocation of PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE memory, generally at offset 0x20000000, with a valid PE header and known strings present.
